The only decisions layer 3 still needs from the owner, one row each, from `v2/docs/handover/layer3/l3r2.yaml`; every figure is a model or desk result of the records named on `L3-RECONCILIATION.md`, not a measurement, and nothing here is drawn, built or tested. A recommendation is the session's and is not an approval (D-21): each row stays AWAITING until the owner's own words decide it. Rows L3-OD1, L3-OD2, L3-OD4 and L3-OD6 were held by the owner's review (D-22), his instruction on this table (D-23) and his addendum (D-24) until the checked energy basis and the checked power path were filed. Both are, bound to the tip `cd8720a1ab6e` of stream l3plane that their accepted check names (`v2/docs/records/l3r2/checks/energy-basis-check-5/CHECK-5.md`), and every figure on these rows is that basis's, linked to its section. Row L3-OD7, M1's runtime, comes first (D-27, the owner: "Evaluate alternatives before asking me to sacrifice functions or accept restrictive deployment conditions."): rows L3-OD1, L3-OD2, L3-OD4 and L3-OD6 are not asked before it is answered, their scripts refuse until it is, and its figures are the bounded runtime and battery comparison of stream l3batt, bound to the tip `63897fc31c4b` its accepted check names (`v2/docs/records/l3r5/checks/l3batt-check-3/CHECK-3.md`).

Changes to weather coverage, deployment restrictions, functionality, operating conditions, enclosure constraints, mission requirements, charging time or approved resources are proposals for the owner's explicit decision (D-22 to D-25): each appears only as a row or an option he answers, naming the requirement it changes with the consequence quantified (each row's owner test), never as a closure, and none is taken because the current design passes it. ## The closure (D-28, D-29): the owner decision left

None. CFL-017 was the only candidate for a contradiction between mandatory owner requirements; on D-29 it is a collision between the requirements and the current cell, an engineering selection (cell_provenance), so the requirements are coherent and FEA-008 carries the obligation to layer 4. What remains the owner's is an approval, not a decision: the definition re-issue's change record (L3-C26) and his acceptance of the baseline, after the independent check of this closure (L3-C27).

**The modelled baseline (D-28).** The present candidates miss the 48 to 72 hour objective even without tablet charging. With HF and the tablet kept, battery-only from full: D-06's ruled 4S3P pack runs 2.52 h at +20 C (1.04 h at -10 C); the studied in-case candidate, Option A(i)'s base 4S6P and a 4S9P lid (544.4 Wh usable aged at +20 C), runs 12.71 h (5.24 h at -10 C). Solar-assisted on SC-37's mean day, one plane 40 degrees facing south, TYP: D-06's pack does not carry a night (it allows at most 9.1 W for M1 against 42.8 W); the studied candidate stops at 05 UTC of the first night, hour 23 from a 06 UTC start and hour 11 from an 18 UTC start, as drawn (266.7 Wh unserved at 48 h, 494.7 Wh at 72 h) and on the hypothetical corrected path alike (102.2 Wh at 48 h, 165.7 Wh at 72 h, NOM), in 0 of 864 past September windows. The corrected path is not implemented. Optional tablet charging and HF listening reduce endurance further, which the owner accepts (D-28). This is design risk DR-01, assigned to layer 4; REQ-072 reads FAIL at desk.

Definitions 1b and 3, and feasibility items FI-02 and FI-06, rest on the bounded feasibility record [L3-FEASIBILITY.md](../../records/l3feas/L3-FEASIBILITY.md) of stream l3feas at `c11b99d33015`: bound to that tip and accepted by its check `v2/docs/records/l3r5/checks/l3feas-check-2/CHECK-2.md`, every file byte identical to the tip's. Its checks, filed byte for byte: [CHECK-1.md](../../records/l3r5/checks/l3feas-check-1/CHECK-1.md), of stream l3feas, fnd/l3feas at 24942a5f, NOT_ACCEPTED; [CHECK-2.md](../../records/l3r5/checks/l3feas-check-2/CHECK-2.md), of stream l3feas, fnd/l3feas at c11b99d3, ACCEPTED.

**1b. M1's pass line at the kit loads** (row L3-OD1, REQ-072; `od_l3_1.py (approve)`)

The specified service continues for 72 hours within voltage, power and pack limits; combined stored energy alone is not the line. On the reference case stated exactly (L3-FEASIBILITY.md section 2, checked by CHECK-2 of stream l3feas): both packs full and aged at the start (80 percent of the cells' specification minimum), the base pack at +20 C and the lid pack at the reference day's lowest air, 13.23 C; the load PS-IDLE-SPEC, 42.8 W at the pack terminals, plus the lid path's standby drain, split between the packs by capacity; ONE benchmark plane, 40 degrees of slope facing south at Leiden, the single exact orientation while no deployment band is established; the installation row L3-OD6 names (TYP or WAB); each pack's cutoff its graceful line (5 percent relative state of charge, or its lowest cell at 3.00 V under load), the kit's shutdown the base pack at its line; the power-path case the corrected path (case (iii), HYPOTHETICAL). Four conditions, all required: (1) every hour of the 72 serves the load, each pack drawn only to its own line; (2) the lowest store of the pack or packs still able to carry the kit stays above 4.2 Wh; (3) every path within its limits every hour (the lid path under its 8.7 A minimum; the charge currents within U3's 3.968 A, U3B's 7.936 A and the cells' REQ-075 current); (4) the node at or above every load converter's minimum input with the base pack at 12.0 V, an engineering obligation no record reads yet. On the studied candidate conditions 1 and 2 are modelled, condition 3 INFERRED and condition 4 not established. After a permitted pack cutoff the remaining supply carries the loads.

**The owner's choice:** the owner's sub-choice 1b (od_l3_1.py --pass-line): `kit-loads`, the four conditions (the review's criterion, recommended), or `each-pack`, condition (2) held by each pack alone (stricter; no route of the studied candidate meets it in WAB, hf_wab.out 1)

**3. The solar topology apart from its electrical compliance** (row L3-OD3, REQ-016; `od_l3_3.py`)

The owner's answer sets the topology, the voltage class and the installation condition (REQ-016); it verifies no rating. The interface is stated quantity by quantity with its derivation or obligation (L3-FEASIBILITY.md section 3b, checked by CHECK-2 of stream l3feas): the available array power; the converter's input power, NOT controlled as drawn (O-2); the cold open-circuit exposure, 56.25 V by the 1.25 clause on the held sheet (O-3); the short-circuit and fault currents (O-4); the string versus combined-feed protection (O-5); F2 at 20 A and at least 56.25 V DC with its interrupting rating (O-6); the lead, J_SOLAR and the wall's solar pair at 20 A or more (O-7); and the panel revision pinned (O-1: the held sheet has no revision mark; closed when the maker's sheet for the revision bought is filed with its revision mark and sha256, array_calc.py is re-run on it and the set point and voltage basis re-derived).

**4b. The open kit's stability: its full test conditions** (row L3-OD4, REQ-078; `od_l3_4.py (adopt, --push-n)`)

The push is a design target the owner chooses (10 N is proposed as one, not a standard). Application point and direction: at the tablet's far edge, normal to its screen, where the lid carries the tablet; at the QMX set's controls, horizontal and backward, where it carries the QMX; the lower of the two where it carries both. Duration: a static push (the mechanical result is a static moment balance); the test's hold time is a TEST-PLAN item owed. Slope: toward the hinge side, the lid's figure from the mechanical record (feet-inboard bound) or the owner's. Support surface: a rigid flat surface, the case on its feet, their place measured by T-A1-3. Lid angle: 100 degrees on the stay. Load configuration: the lid pack and lid items fitted, the base contents at the swept case's lightest. The candidate's status is the mechanical result that matches these conditions (a1mech README section 5); none is filed for a push on the slope, so no modelled PASS is stated until it is.

**5. The mode-specific environment table** (row L3-OD5, CFL-017 and REQ-051; `od_l3_5.py (reading-c)`)

The selected cell's limits (the Samsung INR18650-35E, Ver. 1.1 as the registry carries it): charge 0 to +45 C and discharge -10 to +60 C at the cell surface (REQ-046); storage -20 to +45 C for up to three months and -20 to +25 C for up to a year (REQ-025); never above +60 C or below -20 C at the cells, the pack out and stored apart for such exposure (REQ-074).

| Mode | Environment | Functions available | Source |

| operation, pack fitted | -20 to +40 C in use, the cells held inside their charge and discharge limits | every function; charge held off outside the cells' charge window; the reduced mode, the heat stage and the hot stop act on the measured temperatures (CONOPS section 4c) | REQ-046, REQ-051 |
| storage and transport, pack fitted | -20 to +45 C for three months, -20 to +25 C for a year; never above +60 C or below -20 C at the cells | none: the pack in its gauge's shutdown | REQ-025, REQ-074 |

It costs no parts or money; it reduces the claimed capability, and the owner's acceptance covers that reduction.

## Applying an answer

Each row has a prepared registry restatement, not applied: `python3 v2/docs/records/l3r2/conditional/<script> --option <option> --words "<the owner's words>" --date <YYYY-MM-DD>` records his answer as an owner ruling that names the row and applies the exact registry change; `--check` does the same in memory and writes nothing. A row whose `requires` is not met is refused. After a script: `rules_lib.py requirements`, `rules_render.py --requirements` and this renderer.

## Requirements that cannot both hold: the only answers refused (D-26)

The prepared scripts refuse an answer only where two rulings would set requirements that cannot both hold, and the completion gate reads the target unambiguous only when none does. A combination whose studied candidate fails is not among them: it records a feasibility item (the owner's reviewer: "A combination can be a valid target and have a FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE implementation").

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| row L3-OD2 is not answered while row L3-OD1 stands rejected | every option of row L3-OD2 sets a lid pack (4S15P, 4S14P or 4S9P), and a reject keeps D-06's one pack: the two requirements cannot both hold, so row L3-OD2 does not apply after a reject (od_l3_2.py refuses; the gate counts the row as not applicable) |
| row L3-OD4's adopt carries a plane band only with row L3-OD3's array and row L3-OD6's weather basis the band was derived for | a band is a grid's result for one array on one day; with another array or a coverage target the two requirements cannot both hold. No band exists at U3's 6.0 A bracket (ENERGY-BASIS.md section 1), so adopt carries only the open kit's stability and this rule binds nothing today |
| row L3-OD6 decided on its table while row L3-OD7 sets 48 hours or the HF receiver on | row L3-OD6's table sizes the store for 72-hour windows at the approved profile; with 48 hours required or the receiver's 1.14 W added the two requirements cannot both hold, so row L3-OD6 is restated from the runtime comparison first (od_l3_6.py refuses; D-27, closure item L3-C56) |
| row L3-OD2 answered qmx-out while row L3-OD7 sets the HF receiver listening through M1 | the receiver cannot listen through M1 in a kit that carries no HF set: the two requirements cannot both hold (od_l3_2.py refuses; D-27). With HF available, qmx-out stays the owner's to choose, revisiting D-27's 'preserve HF' |
| one ruling on the array | row L3-OD1 fixes no array; row L3-OD3 alone does, and od_l3_3.py replaces REQ-072's marked phrase with it, or adds it as a note where row L3-OD1 was rejected |
